questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Hornfels is a fine-grained, massive rock produced by which type of metamorphism?
options: Coarse-grained, banded rock from regional metamorphism at depth
Friction-melt glass produced along faults during earthquakes
Fine-grained, massive. Contact metamorphic. Spotted variety
Foliated rock with visible mica flakes formed at medium grade
questions.solution: Hornfels: baked rock near intrusion. Granofels: massive granoblastic texture.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Spinel lherzolite is considered representative of which region of the Earth?
questions.solution: Spinel lherzolite: olivine + orthopyroxene + clinopyroxene + spinel. Dominant upper mantle rock. Found as xenoliths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is an igneous rock composed of more than 50% carbonate minerals?
options: Sedimentary limestone formed by accumulation of calcareous shell debris
Metamorphic marble produced by contact metamorphism of limestone
Silicate igneous rock in which quartz and feldspar are the dominant phases
questions.solution: Carbonatite: rare, mantle-derived. Contains REE, Nb, P. Example: Oldoinyo Lengai.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The GASP geobarometer, sensitive to pressure, is based on which net-transfer reaction?
options: Fe-Mg exchange between garnet and biotite giving an independent temperature estimate for the same rock
Grossular + Al₂SiO₅ + Quartz → Anorthite. Pressure-sensitive. Used with Grt-Bt thermometer
Aluminum saturation index of the bulk rock used to infer crystallization depth of the source magma
Si-content of phengite calibrated as a temperature-dependent barometer for low-grade pelitic schists
questions.solution: GASP: Ca transfer. K = a_An³/(a_Grs·a_Ky²·a_Qz). P from equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, the vector data model represents geographic features using which basic geometric elements together with attributes and topology?
options: Points, lines, polygons. Attributes. Topology (shared boundaries)
A continuous grid of cells, in which each cell holds a single value
Points and lines only; polygons are not supported within vector GIS models
Polygons without topology, so that the shared boundaries are duplicated
questions.solution: Vector: precise, less storage (simple features). Topology: arc-node structure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a deep sea fan facies model, the inner, mid, and outer fan zones are distinguished by which deposits and sedimentary structures?
options: Coastal system of beaches, barriers and washover fans
Continental shelf with storm-reworked sand ridges, tidal sand waves and the thick muddy offshore shelf deposits
Inner fan (channel + levee), Mid fan (suprafan lobes), Outer fan (thin-bedded turbidites). Bouma Ta-e cycles
River-dominated delta with mouth bars and distributary channels
questions.solution: Deep fan: suprafan = depositional lobe. Channel avulsion. Growth faulting on slope.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which end-member compositions make up the solid solution series of the garnet group?
options: Only the pyrope end-member is present in all natural garnet compositions
Only the almandine end-member occurs in metamorphic rocks
Only the grossular end-member is stable at high pressure
questions.solution: Garnet: X₃Y₂(SiO₄)₃. X = Fe²⁺, Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺. Y = Al³⁺, Fe³⁺.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Limestone is composed predominantly of the mineral:
questions.solution: Limestone is a carbonate rock chiefly of calcite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+25+10) = 57%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Back-arc basin formation: extension behind volcanic arc:
options: Caused by collision of a continental fragment with the volcanic arc
Caused by ridge subduction and the opening of a slab window beneath the arc
Caused by crustal thickening due to compressional forces at the margin
Caused by rollback of subducting slab or mantle wedge convection
questions.solution: Back-arc: Sea of Japan, Philippine Sea. Extension: graben, new ocean floor. Volcanic arc on upper plate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Volcanism above a subduction zone characteristically produces magmas of which composition?
options: Tholeiitic basalts of the mid-ocean ridge type
Ultramafic komatiite lavas of the Archean
questions.solution: Subduction: flux melting from released water. Volcanic arcs.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Trilobites are index fossils mainly for which era, and which genera characterize the Lower, Middle, and Upper subdivisions?
options: Jurassic index fossils. Dactylioceras, Hildoceras and Parkinsonia define the standard zonal scheme. Extinct at the end-Jurassic
Cretaceous index fossils. Inoceramus and ammonites of the chalk define the zonal scheme
Cambrian index fossils. Redlichia (Lower Cambrian), Paradoxides (Middle), Olenus (Upper). Extinct end-Permian
Devonian index fossils. Phacops and Dalmanites dominate reefs. Extinct end-Devonian
questions.solution: Trilobites: Arthropoda. Cephalon + thorax + pygidium. Holaspid (adult) segments vary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Stromatolites preserved in the rock record represent what kind of ancient structures?
options: Skeletal remains of early shelly invertebrates
Trace fossils of burrowing marine arthropods
Abiogenic chemical precipitates of marine carbonate
questions.solution: Stromatolites: layered structures from cyanobacteria. Oldest evidence of life (~3.5 Ga). Still form today in Shark Bay.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Hydrothermal alteration zoning in porphyry copper:
options: Potassic → phyllic → argillic → propylitic (outward from center)
Random distribution of alteration minerals without any spatial relationship to the intrusion
Propylitic alteration in the core grading outward to potassic at the margins
A single uniform alteration assemblage throughout the entire intrusive body
questions.solution: Potassic: K-feldspar, biotite. Phyllic: sericite, quartz, pyrite. Argillic: clay. Propylitic: chlorite, epidote.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Argon-40/Argon-39 dating is a variant of:
options: U-Pb dating of zircon and other uranium minerals
Rb-Sr dating of whole-rock mineral isochrons
Sm-Nd dating of mafic and ultramafic rocks
questions.solution: 40Ar/39Ar: irradiation converts 39K to 39Ar. Single sample, step-heating. Gives age spectrum and identifies excess Ar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Calc-silicate rocks, containing minerals like diopside and wollastonite, form by metamorphism of:
options: Metamorphosed quartz sandstone composed almost entirely of quartz grains
Serpentinized ultramafic rock containing chrysotile and amphibole asbestos
Metamorphosed impure limestone/dolomite. Diopside, wollastonite, grossular
Pure carbonate rock that recrystallized without forming any silicate minerals
questions.solution: Calc-silicate: Ca-Mg silicates from silica + carbonate. Wollastonite: CaSiO3.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The presence of sillimanite in a metamorphic rock indicates what grade of metamorphism?
options: Hydrothermal replacement of feldspar-rich host rock
questions.solution: Sillimanite: Al₂SiO₅ polymorph. Stable at high T. Kyanite (high P), andalusite (low P) are lower grade polymorphs.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the geological nature of the Indo-Gangetic Plain and its sedimentary fill?
options: Rocky terrain composed of exposed Precambrian basement of the Indian Shield
Basement exposed at surface with no sediment cover anywhere in the plain
Thin sedimentary cover resting directly upon the Deccan volcanic pile
Foredeep basin. Thick alluvium (Tertiary-Quaternary). Aquifer system
questions.solution: Alluvium: Bhabhar (piedmont), Tarai (wetland), Bhangar (older), Khadar (younger).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Differential weathering produces landforms such as:
options: Dune fields of migrating desert sand
Paired terraces of a graded river
questions.solution: Differential weathering: varying resistance of rock layers creates isolated landforms. Softer rock erodes faster, harder caprock remains.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do preloading with wick drains accelerate settlement in soft ground?
options: Preloading reduces settlement by permanently increasing the moisture content of the foundation soil
Wick drains act as rigid piles to carry the load without any settlement
Surcharge loading causes immediate undrained failure of the foundation soil
Pre-construction settlement by surcharge + vertical drains. Accelerates consolidation
questions.solution: Wick drains: prefabricated vertical drains (PVD). Spacing 1-3m. Surcharge height ~2-6m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Fold interference patterns — Ramsay types:
options: Only type 1 dome and basin interference occurs during superposed folding of a single generation of folds
Only type 2 boomerang interference occurs during superposed folding
Only type 3 hook interference occurs during superposed folding
Type 0 (no interference), Type 1 (dome-basin), Type 2 (boomerang), Type 3 (hook). Superposed folding
questions.solution: Type 1: F₁ ⊥ F₂. Dome and basin. Type 2: inclined F₁. Boomerang. Type 3: co-axial F₁, F₂.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines the base level of erosion and distinguishes its ultimate from its local forms?
options: The highest elevation that water reaches in the river channel during peak flood discharge events
The highest point of the drainage basin where the process of headward erosion begins
The ridge line separating two adjacent drainage basins that share a common watershed boundary at the ground surface
Lowest level to which a river can erode. Ultimate: sea level. Local: lake, resistant rock
questions.solution: Base level: controls river profile. Changes in base level → aggradation or degradation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In mantle melting models, the difference between batch melting and fractional (Rayleigh) melting is that:
options: No partial melting occurs anywhere in the upper mantle beneath the plates
Batch: complete equilibration. Fractional (Rayleigh): melt removed continuously. Trace element modeling
Only batch melting operates, since melt always equilibrates with its residue
Only fractional melting operates, because melt segregation prevents equilibration with the residue at all depths
questions.solution: Batch: C_l/C_o = 1/(D + F(1-D)). Fractional: C_l/C_o = (1-F)^{(1/D - 1)}/D.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which grouping correctly classifies ore deposit types by their genetic processes?
options: Magmatic (Cr, Pt), Hydrothermal (Cu, Zn, Pb), Sedimentary (Fe, Mn, P), Residual (Al, Ni), Placer (Au, Sn)
All ore deposits are magmatic, forming by crystallization from a cooling silicate melt
All ore deposits are hydrothermal in origin, formed by hot metal-rich waters circulating through the crust and concentrating economic ores
All ore deposits are placers, derived from gravity concentration of heavy mineral grains
questions.solution: Ore: economically extractable. Grade × tonnage. Gangue: waste minerals.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which mining method typically produces a subsidence trough at the surface?
options: Subsidence only occurs at the mine portal and never above the extracted panel area
The ground surface always rises as an uplift dome over the panel
Longwall mining → subsidence trough. Angle of draw. Impact on structures
Roof falls underground are fully unrelated to any surface movement
questions.solution: Subsidence: vertical displacement. Tilt and curvature cause damage. Mitigation: backfill, pillars.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In isotope hydrology, precipitation samples plot on the global meteoric water line; what does deviation from this line indicate?
options: Plot on global meteoric water line (δD = 8δ¹⁸O + 10). Deviation = evaporation
Values of both isotopes are always positive for every natural water sample
The two isotope ratios are identical in every natural water body on Earth
The two isotopes plot randomly with no mathematical relation existing between them
questions.solution: MWL: Craig (1961). Local MWL may differ. Evaporation shifts points below line.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Diffraction: X-rays interact with crystal lattice:
options: Random scattering. X-rays bounce off atoms without any phase relationship
Constructive interference when Bragg's law satisfied (nλ=2d sinθ)
No interaction. X-rays pass through crystals without deviation or diffraction
Absorption only. Crystals absorb X-rays and emit no characteristic scattered beams
questions.solution: Diffraction: crystal as 3D grating. Bragg's law: nλ = 2d sinθ. Peak positions → d-spacings.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 3 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 1.3 (in the given time units). Its age is:
questions.solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 3×1.3 = 3.9.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In which depositional setting does the mineral glauconite most commonly form?
options: Freshwater lake deltas with rapid sedimentation and oxygenated bottom waters
Shallow marine, reducing conditions, slow sedimentation
Deep-ocean floor with abundant terrigenous clastic input and fast accumulation rates
Arid desert plains with wind-blown sand and ephemeral flash-flood channels
questions.solution: Glauconite: green mineral. Forms in marine environments with low sedimentation rates.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS polygon overlay, which set of operations, including intersect, union, clip, and erase, is performed between data layers?
options: Merge and dissolve operations within a single layer only
Intersect, union, clip, erase operations between layers
Spatial join of attributes onto points, lines and polygons
Visual overlay with no attribute or geometry processing
questions.solution: Overlay: combines spatial data. Intersect: AND. Union: OR. Erase: NOT. Clip: restrict to boundary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which combination of indicators indicates overexploitation of a groundwater aquifer?
options: Rising water levels with falling pumping costs and no change in water quality
Declining water levels, increasing pumping cost, land subsidence, saltwater intrusion
A gradual increase in rainfall and a continuously rising river stage in the basin
Increased baseflow contribution to streams along with a steadily rising potentiometric surface
questions.solution: Overabstraction: cone of depression expands, baseflow reduction, ecological impacts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gas content of a coal seam is commonly measured in the laboratory using which method?
options: Desorption canister method. Measure gas released over time, extrapolate to total gas
Downhole geophysical logging of coal beds to estimate gas pressure and saturation trends
Seismic refraction profiling of the seam to infer zones of high gas content
Direct drilling of the seam followed by open-hole permeability testing only
questions.solution: Canister: sealed coal sample, measure desorbed gas. Extrapolate using √t or diffusion model.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 45° shows a width of 20 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 20×sin45° ≈ 14.14 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On a stereographic projection, what does the pole to a plane represent for a geological surface?
options: The great circle that represents the full three-dimensional orientation of the plane on the net
The line of maximum dip of the plane drawn as a tick mark on a geological map
The intersection point of the plane with the line of the strike measured in the field
Point on stereonet representing plane orientation (dip direction and amount)
questions.solution: Pole: perpendicular to plane. Contoured for density analysis (π-diagrams).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which unconformity shows parallel beds above and below an erosional surface representing a gap in time?
options: Beds above the erosional surface are tilted at a high angle relative to beds below the surface
Parallel beds above and below erosional surface (missing time)
Sedimentary beds rest directly on eroded crystalline igneous or metamorphic rocks
The contact is a conformable one in which no time gap is present in the record
questions.solution: Disconformity: missing strata due to erosion. Hard to recognize in field.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In terms of relative age, what do the cores of anticlines and synclines contain?
options: Youngest rocks occur in the core of an anticline and oldest in the core of a syncline
There is no consistent age relation between fold type and the age of the core rocks
Oldest rocks in core of anticline. Youngest in core of syncline
Both folds place the oldest rocks in their cores regardless of their geometric shape
questions.solution: Anticline: upfold. Syncline: downfold. Recumbent: axial plane nearly horizontal.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 30 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(30/10) ≈ 71.6°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 10 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/10 = 4.5 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an unconfined aquifer, the water table is the boundary between the:
options: Boundary between saturated and unsaturated zones. Fluctuates with recharge
Upper surface of the confining bed that caps the aquifer beneath the zone
Level at which water stands in a well drilled into a confined aquifer body
Zone of permanent saturation that lies below the regional water table surface
questions.solution: Water table: follows topography. Perched water table: above regional water table.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral that effervesces (fizzes) when dilute hydrochloric acid is applied is:
questions.solution: Calcite (CaCO₃) reacts with dilute HCl, releasing CO₂ — a standard field test.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What evidence and techniques are used to correlate buried river channels and river terraces of different ages?
options: Buried channels mapped by geophysics. Terraces coded QTI (oldest) to QTIV (youngest). Tectonic/climatic
Buried channels can be detected only where they crop out at the present land surface and mapped on the ground directly by surveyors
Abandoned channels and river terraces can be correlated only on the basis of their fossil content
Relict channels and terraces are visible only on high-resolution aerial photography of the drainage basin
questions.solution: Paleochannel: potential aquifer. Terrace: abandoned floodplain. Stratigraphic marker.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Unsupervised classification groups pixels by:
options: Manual interpretation by a skilled photo-interpreter
Predefined classes provided by the analyst before running
Field survey points collected using handheld GPS units
questions.solution: Unsupervised: ISODATA, K-means algorithms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On what parameter is NEHRP seismic site classification based?
options: Classes are based only on the depth of the water table at the site
Classification uses peak ground acceleration at the bedrock level only for the site
A (hard rock) to F (liquefiable). Vs30 (shear wave velocity in top 30m)
Site classes depend on the magnitude of the design earthquake only

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: IUGS classification: QAPF diagram for plutonic rocks. Granite fields:
options: Plagioclase exceeding alkali feldspar with quartz greater than twenty percent
Quartz less than twenty percent with plagioclase exceeding alkali feldspar
Feldspathoids present and quartz completely absent from the modal analysis
questions.solution: QAPF: modal mineralogy. Granite: Q 20-60%, A>P. Granodiorite: P>A. Tonalite: P>>A.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the stratigraphic position, lithology, and fossil content of the Lameta Formation?
options: Supratrappean (above the Deccan) marine sediments with abundant foraminifera tests
Infratrappean (below Deccan). Freshwater limestone, sandstone. Dinosaur fossils
Intertrappean lacustrine beds interlayered within the main basalt flows of the pile
Post-Deccan lateritic capping formed by intense tropical weathering of the basalt
questions.solution: Lameta: Maastrichtian age. Dinosaur nesting site (Jabalpur). Paleoenvironment: fluvial-lacustrine.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sub-environments and bedding features are typical of the tidal flat facies?
options: Uniform coarse sand with large-scale trough cross-bedding and no fine-grained intervals
Mudflat (clay), mixed flat (mud+sand), sandflat (sand). Bioturbation, flaser bedding
Thick organic-rich peat accumulating in anoxic coastal swamps with root traces
Pure laminated clay with no sand layers, formed in a deep, quiet-water basin
questions.solution: Tidal flat: laminae (sand-mud couplets). Flaser, wavy, lenticular bedding. Tidal channels.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which minerals are characteristically stable in the granulite facies, where hydrous minerals become unstable?
options: Hornblende + biotite + epidote. Hydrous minerals remain perfectly stable
Assemblages rich in amphibole and biotite that remain stable at high water pressures
Chlorite + muscovite + quartz typical of low-grade regional metamorphism
Pyroxene + feldspar + garnet. No hydrous minerals (biotite, amphibole unstable)
questions.solution: Granulite: high T, moderate P. Dehydration melting. Orthopyroxene in mafic rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Magnetic anomaly over dike: symmetric vs asymmetric:
options: Dipping dike gives a symmetric anomaly over its center line
Both vertical and dipping dikes give anomalies over the top edge
Vertical dike: symmetric anomaly. Dipping dike: asymmetric
A vertical dike yields a magnetic low that mirrors the country rock
questions.solution: Dike: magnetic body. Vertical: peak over center. Dipping: peak shifted toward dip direction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Placer gold deposits form by which concentration process operating in streams?
options: Mechanical concentration by gravity in stream sediment
Chemical precipitation of gold from dilute meteoric ground water solutions
Direct condensation of gold vapour from subaerial volcanic eruption clouds
Metamorphic segregation of gold into banded quartz veins during regional metamorphism
questions.solution: Placer: gold concentrated by density in alluvial environments.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rb-Sr isochron method: slope of isochron gives:
options: Age of rock (from ⁸⁷Rb/⁸⁶Sr vs ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr)
Temperature of crystallization of the rock
Pressure of metamorphism of the rock
Initial Sr ratio of the enclosing magma
questions.solution: Isochron: slope = e^{λt}-1. Initial ratio: y-intercept. Good for igneous rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does apparent dip compare with true dip, and which direction does true dip measure on a plane?
options: True dip: angle measured along the strike. Apparent dip: angle measured down the slope
Apparent dip is always greater than the true dip for any direction off the strike line
True and apparent dips are always identical in value in every direction of measurement
True dip: maximum slope. Apparent dip: any other direction (less than true)
questions.solution: True dip: perpendicular to strike. Apparent dip: trigonometric relation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+35+20) = 41%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock sample of 100 cm³ contains 30 cm³ of pore space. Its porosity is:
questions.solution: Porosity = (void volume/total volume)×100 = 30/100 = 30%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which chemical composition corresponds to pyrope, a member of the garnet group of minerals?
questions.solution: Pyrope: Mg-garnet. Found in kimberlite (mantle-derived). Indicator for diamonds.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes a ria, a drowned river valley, from a fjord, a drowned glacial trough?
options: Ria is a valley carved and later drowned by glacial ice
Fjord is a river valley that has been drowned by rising sea level
Ria and fjord are both formed by identical coastal processes
Ria: drowned river valley. Fjord: drowned glacial trough
questions.solution: Ria: dendritic coastline. Fjord: steep-sided, U-shaped. Both are submergent coastlines.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS spatial analysis, a buffer operation creates what around a feature at a specified distance for proximity analysis?
options: Union of all overlapping features into a single layer
Point-in-polygon test for locating sample locations
Intersection of two layers preserving common areas
questions.solution: Buffer: around fault (setback), around river (flood zone). Variable buffer widths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Dilatancy angle ψ: relationship to friction angle φ in rock mechanics:
options: ψ = φ (dilatancy exactly equals the friction angle)
ψ = 2φ (dilatancy is twice the friction angle)
ψ = φ/2 (dilatancy is half the friction angle)
questions.solution: Dilatancy: volume increase during shear. ψ < φ. For sand ψ ≈ φ-30°. Peak: ψ + φ.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which dark, mafic rock is porphyritic with mica and amphibole phenocrysts?
options: Dark, mafic. Porphyritic with mica and amphibole phenocrysts
Light-coloured rock free of phenocrysts and rich in quartz and feldspar
Felsic rock with phenocrysts of quartz, sanidine and plagioclase
Quartz-rich rock consisting largely of quartz, K-feldspar and muscovite
questions.solution: Lamprophyre: high volatile content. Mica and amphibole in groundmass of feldspar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are rock units classified and ranked in the discipline of lithostratigraphy?
options: Division of rocks based only on their structural and tectonic features
Subdivision of the rock column on the basis of measured absolute ages
Correlation of strata on the basis of their contained fossil content
Rock units based on lithology (Formation, Member, Group)
questions.solution: Formation: mappable unit. Member: subdivision. Group: several formations.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sequence of diagenetic modifications is observed in the petrography of carbonate sands?
options: Early marine cementation followed by extensive dissolution of grains, with no evidence of microboring or prioritization at any stage
Mechanical compaction alone, causing grain suturing and pressure solution without any cement precipitation
Rapid total dolomitization of all grains and matrix during shallow burial diagenesis
Micrite envelope (microboring of grains) → prioritization → cementation (meniscus, pendant, blocky)
questions.solution: Micrite envelopes: formed by algal/fungal boring. Phreatic (blocky) vs vadose (meniscus) cement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Schistosity, seen in medium-grade metamorphic rocks, is defined by the alignment of which minerals?
options: Coarse segregation into alternating light and dark mineral layers
Platy mineral alignment (micas) in medium-grade metamorphic rocks
Planar fabric in low-grade slates oriented perpendicular to compression
Lineation defined by alignment of elongate mineral prisms and needles
questions.solution: Schistosity: mica alignment. Schist: medium grade, visible mica flakes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic refraction — critical refraction:
options: Direct arrival that travels entirely within the surface layer after reflection at the boundary
Wave reflected from the interface returned to the surface at an angle equal to the incident angle
Surface wave travelling along the ground with velocity independent of layer properties
Head wave at critical angle (sin i_c = V₁/V₂). Refractor velocity V₂ from intercept time
questions.solution: Refraction: first arrivals. Crossover distance. Layer thickness: h = (x_c/2)√((V₂-V₁)/(V₂+V₁)).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the block diagram shown, the inclined bedding plane dips at 20°. The dip direction is, by definition:
options: Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent
Parallel to the strike, measured along the line of the bedding plane outcrop at the surface
Horizontal along the strike in whatever direction the bedding plane is gently inclined
Vertical regardless of the strike, so dip direction always points straight downward
questions.solution: Dip (here 20°) is measured perpendicular to strike, down the line of steepest slope of the plane.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tritium (³H) is used in groundwater age dating because its half-life and decay signature indicate:
options: Tritium decays with a half-life of about twenty thousand years for dating
Half-life 12.3 years. Indicates recharge after 1953 (nuclear testing)
Tritium is stable and accumulates steadily within an aquifer
Tritium levels date water recharged during the last glacial period
questions.solution: ³H: radioactive tracer. Post-1953 tritium bomb pulse. Combined with ³He for younger waters.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Freeze-thaw, frost heave, solifluction and ice-wedge growth are the characteristic processes operating in which environment?
options: Processes that operate only beneath an active glacier ice mass at the surface
Weathering and erosion processes typical of hot humid tropical rainforest regions
Freeze-thaw, frost heave, solifluction, ice wedges. Patterned ground
Processes dominated by wind erosion and salt weathering in hot desert environments
questions.solution: Periglacial: tundra. Permafrost: perennially frozen ground. Active layer: seasonal thaw.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rockfall protection: catch fence design considers:
options: Only the fence height and the total length of the fence built along the slope
Block energy (kinetic energy at impact), bounce height, runout distance
Only the weight of the largest block in the rockfall source zone
Only the material of the fence posts and their surface finish
questions.solution: Energy: E = ½mv². Height of fence > bounce height. Catch ditch behind fence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Delta progradation: coarsening-upward sequence:
options: prodelta mud → delta front sand → distributary channel sand → coastal plain
Delta front sand → prodelta mud → coastal plain → distributary channel sand, a fining-upward stack
Coastal plain → distributary channel → delta front → prodelta mud, coarsening upward throughout
Uniform fine mud throughout with no coarsening, deposited in a starved basin
questions.solution: Prograding delta: bottom-up = distal to proximal. Coarsening-upward = typical delta sequence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the block diagram shown, the inclined bedding plane dips at 60°. The dip direction is, by definition:
options: Vertical regardless of the strike, so dip direction always points straight downward
Parallel to the strike, measured along the line of the bedding plane outcrop at the surface
Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent
Horizontal along the strike in whatever direction the bedding plane is gently inclined
questions.solution: Dip (here 60°) is measured perpendicular to strike, down the line of steepest slope of the plane.

figure.caption: Strike and dip of a bed

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Glacial buzzsaw hypothesis: glacial erosion limited by:
options: Mean annual temperature of the surrounding region
Total annual snowfall accumulation in the region
The resistance of the bedrock to glacial erosion
questions.solution: Buzzsaw: glacial erosion fastest near ELA. Summits eroded to ELA height.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Walther's law states that facies occurring in a conformable vertical succession also occur:
options: Never side by side in the same basin at any single moment of time
In the reverse order when traced laterally across the basin margin
In a random order without any relation to their vertical stacking pattern
Laterally adjacent in the original depositional environments
questions.solution: Conformably superposed facies represent environments that were originally side by side and migrated.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which structural group of silicate minerals does biotite belong?
questions.solution: Biotite — black mica. One perfect basal cleavage. Common in granite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Quaternary stratigraphy: Marine Isotope Stages (MIS):
options: Oxygen isotope record from foraminifera. Odd = warm, Even = cold
All stages record identical conditions with no climate fluctuation at all
No correlation exists between isotope stages and the glacial-interglacial record
Random oscillation driven entirely by local tectonic subsidence in the basin
questions.solution: MIS: marine cores. MIS 1 = Holocene. MIS 2 = Last Glacial Maximum. MIS 5e = Last Interglacial.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which type of twinning is commonly observed in the mineral orthoclase feldspar?
questions.solution: Orthoclase: K-feldspar. Carlsbad: composition plane (010).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 20 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The Darcy velocity is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What kind of twin does the Carlsbad law produce in orthoclase feldspar?
options: Polysynthetic lamellar twinning repeated across many lamellae
Simple contact twin in orthoclase. Two individuals
Albite twin law producing thin parallel lamellae in plagioclase
Pericline twinning with the composition plane (001) in microcline
questions.solution: Carlsbad: common in orthoclase. Simple twin with composition plane (010).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Remote sensing for geology: lineament analysis identifies:
options: Only vegetation density and land use categories
Linear thermal anomalies, not structural geological features
Stream network order and drainage basin boundaries
Faults, fractures, joints, dikes, lithological boundaries
questions.solution: Lineaments: linear features from satellite imagery. Structural control. Mineralization often associated.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pediment vs alluvial fan: pediment is bedrock surface, fan is sediment deposit:
options: Pediment: bedrock, gentle slope. Fan: alluvial cone at mountain front
A pediment is a depositional surface built of alluvial sediment at the mountain front
An alluvial fan is an erosional surface cut into solid bedrock
Pediment and alluvial fan are the same landform with different names
questions.solution: Pediment: etched bedrock surface. Fan: depositional. Pediment may have thin alluvial cover.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 50 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×50 = 500000 m³ = 0.5 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a ductile shear zone, what do S-foliation and C-foliation represent, and what does their mutual angle indicate?
options: S-foliation (flattening), C-foliation (shear). Angle indicates shear sense
S-foliation is parallel to the shear zone boundary and C-foliation lies at 45° to it
Both S and C foliations are always perpendicular to each other at a fixed right angle
The angle between S and C fabrics remains constant and carries no shear-sense information
questions.solution: S-C: S (45° to shear), C (parallel). Type I (S-C mylonites). Type II (S-C' in S-C mylonites).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In mineralogy, crystal field theory is used to explain which properties of transition metal minerals?
options: Cleavage directions related to weak bond planes in minerals
Bond length variations caused by cation substitution in silicates
Color and magnetic properties of transition metal minerals
Hardness differences arising from framework tetrahedral linkage
questions.solution: Crystal field: d-orbital splitting. Color: d-d transitions. Magnetic: unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater occurrence in hard rock terrains is primarily controlled by:
options: Water in hard rocks occurs only within primary intergranular pores between mineral grains
Fracture-controlled. Weathered zone (shallow) + fractured zone (deeper). Yield variable
The rock mass behaves as a porous medium with a uniform and very high storage capacity
Yield is uniform everywhere and entirely independent of the fracture network
questions.solution: Hard rock: only secondary porosity. Fracture zones, lineaments. High-yield wells along major fractures.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (10+20+8) = 62%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 45° shows a width of 10 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 10×sin45° ≈ 7.07 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Indian Gondwana stratigraphy: Lower Gondwana coal-bearing:
options: Talchir boulder bed with glacial striations at the base of the entire Gondwana pile
Panchet red beds with the earliest Triassic vertebrate fauna of peninsular India
Raniganj arkose and shale deposited in a marine shelf environment in the Damodar valley
questions.solution: Karharbari: early Permian, good coal. Barakar: major coal seams. Talchir: glacial.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Landslide remediation: rock bolts provide:
options: Only re-distribution of surface loads by concreting the slope face
Removal of the overburden to reduce the gravitational driving force acting on the entire slope
Active reinforcement by compressing rock mass and increasing frictional resistance
Blanket drainage of all the groundwater by horizontal filter drains
questions.solution: Rock bolts: grouted or mechanical. Passive: resist movement. Active: pre-tensioned to compress.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: For a geological cross-section to be considered balanced, what condition must be satisfied during restoration?
options: Conservation of bed length alone, ignoring any changes in the area of individual layers
Uniform horizontal shortening applied equally to every layer in the section without pinning
Conservation of bed length and area during restoration
Restoration with gap formation permitted in the synclines and fold crests of the section
questions.solution: Balanced: no gaps or overlaps after restoration. Bed length and area preserved.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the repeating structural unit of the double chain in amphibole silicates?
options: Si₂O₇ isolated double tetrahedra sharing one apex only
Si₄O₁₁⁶⁻ repeating unit. Two pyroxene chains linked
Si₄O₁₀ single rings of four linked tetrahedra
SiO₄ independent tetrahedra isolated from each other
questions.solution: Amphibole: double chain inosilicate. Perfect 56°/124° cleavage. OH in structure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A perched water table forms when a low-permeability lens creates:
options: Local saturated zone above region water table due to low-permeability lens
The regional water table surface that lies within a low permeability rock basin
An unsaturated interval lying directly beneath the regional water table
The piezometric surface of a deeply buried confined aquifer system
questions.solution: Perched: clay lens creates local saturation. Limited yield. Shallow wells.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Granulite facies metamorphism occurs under what approximate temperature and pressure, and with which mineral assemblage?
options: T < 300°C, low P. Hydrous minerals such as chlorite and muscovite stable
Very high P (>15 kbar), low T. Stable along subduction zones
T 400-500°C, moderate P. Biotite and amphibole remain stable
T > 700°C, P 3-10 kbar. Anhydrous minerals (pyroxene, garnet, feldspar)
questions.solution: Granulite: dry conditions. H₂O absent. Pyroxene + garnet + feldspar. Lower crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of core drilling, and which bit is typically used?
options: Bores only through soil using a rotating hollow-stem auger flight system
Crushes rock by repeated impacts of a heavy falling cutting tool
Uses a percussive chisel with no recovery of a continuous sample
Obtains intact rock core. Diamond bit. Core barrel. HQ, NQ, BQ sizes
questions.solution: Core sizes: HQ (63.5mm), NQ (47.6mm), BQ (36.5mm). Recovery ratio: % core recovered.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The general three-dimensional groundwater flow equation reduces to Laplace's equation under which condition?
options: Darcy's law applied only to horizontal flow, with no variation in head or velocity across space
Steady state conditions require that the storage term in the groundwater flow equation be zero
Transient groundwater flow ignores the storage term and assumes a constant hydraulic conductivity everywhere
questions.solution: Steady: ∂²h/∂x² + ∂²h/∂y² + ∂²h/∂z² = 0 (Laplace). Transient: diffusion equation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which are the major Gondwana sedimentary basins distributed across peninsular India?
options: The Himalayan frontal basins of Kashmir and the Karewa lake deposits
The east coast basins like Cauvery and Krishna-Godavari delta areas
The Bengal basin together with the shallow shelf of the Bay of Bengal
questions.solution: Gondwana: rift basins. Lower Gondwana (Permian): coal measures. Upper Gondwana (Triassic-Jurassic): sandstones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: LiDAR return types: first return = canopy top. Last return =:
options: Tree canopy top surface before penetration
Atmospheric scattering layer above the canopy
questions.solution: LiDAR: multiple returns. First = top. Last = ground (if penetrates canopy). Bare earth model.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What interference colors does quartz typically show in thin section under crossed polars?
options: Black indicating complete extinction in every orientation
Second-order blue typical of very high birefringence
Third-order red characteristic of strongly birefringent minerals
questions.solution: Quartz: low birefringence → grey-white colors under crossed polars. Uniaxial positive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In Miller indices, the notation (hkl) is obtained from what property of crystal faces?
options: Plane angles. (111), (100) and (110) record the interfacial angles between crystal faces
Interaxial angles. The triplets (111), (100) and (110) describe the angular setting of the crystallographic axes
Intercepts on crystal axes. (111): octahedron. (100): cube. (110): dodecahedron. Negative: bar over index
Directions. (111), (100) and (110) give the linear growth direction of crystal edges
questions.solution: Miller: reciprocal of intercepts. Zero = parallel to axis. Dhkl = a/√(h²+k²+l²) (cubic).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a discordant tabular igneous intrusion that cross-cuts bedding?
options: Concordant sheet intrusion emplaced parallel to the bedding planes
Horizontal intrusion that lies parallel to stratification of the host rock
Concordant intrusion that domes the strata above its flat floor
questions.solution: Dyke: vertical or steeply dipping. Radiating or linear swarms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which material property, its resistance to temperature change, is mapped remotely using day-night temperature differences?
options: Resistance to temperature change. High for wet/dense materials. Day-night ΔT for mapping
The rate of heat flow, which depends only upon the surface colour of the material that is involved
A uniform material property of the ground that is identical for all rock types present
Low for wet and dense materials such as water, while high for dry loose sand
questions.solution: Thermal inertia: √(ρ·k·C_p). Quartz: high. Water: very high. Dry sand: low. Used in geology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A reverse (or thrust) fault is produced mainly by:
questions.solution: Compression pushes the hanging wall up over the footwall — a reverse/thrust fault.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, basin setting, and characteristic fossil content of the Siwalik Group?
options: Marine fossils of open-ocean foraminifera deposited in a deep-water shelf setting
Miocene-Pleistocene. Himalayan foreland basin. Fossils: mammals (elephant, horse, ape)
Only volcanic rocks with thick andesitic lava flows and tuff horizons throughout the section
No fossils of any kind due to complete oxidation of the original organic material
questions.solution: Siwalik: sandstone, conglomerate. Himalayan uplift record. Ramapithecus, Sivapithecus.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines drainage density and states the conditions under which it becomes high?
options: The total stream length multiplied by the area of the drainage basin that it drains
The number of streams in a drainage basin divided by the total drainage area of that basin in square kilometres
The drainage basin area divided by the total length of the main stream channel
Total stream length / basin area. High Dd = impermeable rock, high relief, low infiltration
questions.solution: Dd < 5 km/km² (coarse) to > 500 (fine). Lithology and climate control.
